summary: Army Region 1 reported that on the 18th day of conflict, Cambodian forces launched 40 BM-21 rockets into civilian areas of Ban Khlong Phaeng, Sa Kaeo. Over 17,913 Thai residents are currently being sheltered across 40 evacuation centers in 4 border districts.
title: กองทัพภาคที่ 1 สรุปสถานการณ์ชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา พื้นที่ จ.สระแก้ว ประจำวัน 25 ธันวาคม 2568
titleEn: Army Region 1 summarizes Sa Kaeo border situation: 40 BM-21 rockets fired at Thai civilians

summary: The 1st Army Region reported that on the 18th day of the conflict (Dec 25), Cambodian forces fired 40 BM-21 rockets into a civilian residential area at Ban Khlong Phaeng, Ta Phraya District, Sa Kaeo. The attack damaged houses, utilities, and farmland. Currently, 17,913 Thai civilians from four border districts have been evacuated to 40 temporary shelters. The military stated this intentional attack on civilians violates international humanitarian law.
title: กองทัพภาคที่ 1 สรุปเหตุปะทะชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา พื้นที่สระแก้วล่าสุด 25 ธ.ค.68
titleEn: 1st Army Region summarizes Thai-Cambodia border clashes in Sa Kaeo, latest Dec 25, 2025

summary: Brigadier General Sopka Priab stated that Chanthaburi and Pailin are sister cities and that Thailand and Cambodia are neighbors that cannot be separated. Despite ongoing border tensions, he emphasized the goal of peace for the people but declined to provide specifics on the progress or direction of the General Border Committee (GBC) negotiations.
title: นายพลเขมร ย้ำ ไทย-กัมพูชา คือพี่น้อง ต้องพึ่งพาแยกกันไม่ได้ ไม่ตอบทิศทางถก GBC
titleEn: Cambodian General stresses Thailand-Cambodia are brothers, must rely on each other, remains silent on GBC direction

summary: Cambodia requested to delay the GBC secretariat meeting to 18:00 to review Thai proposals. Capt. Yodthanong of the Border Affairs Department stated that the likelihood of a full ministerial meeting on Dec 27 is only '50-50'. Meanwhile, officials at the Chanthaburi-Pailin border confirmed the situation there remains calm despite the wider conflict.
title: เขมรขอเลื่อนถกหยุดยิงเป็น 18.00 น. ทัพไทยเผยโอกาสเจรจายัง 50-50 ยันจันทบุรีไร้ปะทะ
titleEn: Cambodia asks to delay ceasefire talks to 18:00; Thai military says 50-50 chance for success

summary: Front-page news reports that Cambodia is ignoring the General Border Committee (GBC) framework, choosing to continue heavy shelling even as secretariat talks began. The report highlights the emotional story of a Thai soldier who lost his leg but had to hide the news from his bedridden mother. It also features academics urging Cambodians to stop believing government propaganda aimed at inciting hatred toward Thailand.
title: เดลินิวส์ 26 ธ.ค. กัมพูชาเมิน GBC ยิงถล่มต่อ ชายแดนเดือด-ทหารเสียขาที่ 9
titleEn: Daily News Dec 26: Cambodia Ignores GBC, Shelling Continues; Border Intense as 9th Soldier Loses Leg

summary: Officials at the General Border Committee (GBC) meeting in Chanthaburi have drafted a ceasefire agreement set for December 27, 2025. Both sides will monitor the situation for 72 hours while waiting for a final decision from the Thai National Security Council.
title: คาดหยุดยิง 27 ธ.ค.68 ไทยจับตาสถานการณ์ 72 ชั่วโมง รอ สมช.เคาะเย็นนี้
titleEn: Ceasefire expected Dec 27; Thailand monitors for 72 hours awaiting NSC decision

summary: ACM Prapas Sornjaidee, director of the Joint Thai-Cambodian Situation Briefing Centre, stated that Thai military operations are 'strictly defensive' under Article 51 of the UN Charter. Thailand maintains it has no intention of occupying Cambodian territory. Meanwhile, the Army Chief of Staff noted that most military objectives have been achieved, but Thailand insists Cambodia must be the one to formally declare a ceasefire first as they initiated the conflict.
title: Border operations 'strictly defensive'

summary: The Thai Army Region 2 announced that it has regained control over 90% of the disputed sovereign territory. It successfully seized 'Hill 225,' a strategic point near Prasat Ta Kwai that connects to Hill 350. However, a combat engineer sustained a serious injury, losing his left leg to a landmine near the temple, making him the 9th soldier to suffer such an injury in this conflict. The army accuses Cambodia of lacking the intent to stop the conflict, citing continued BM-21 rocket fire into Sa Kaeo.
title: ทัพไทยคุมพื้นที่อธิปไตยแล้ว90% ยึดเนิน225สำเร็จ ทหารช่างเหยียบบึ้มขาขาดรายที่9
titleEn: Thai Military Controls 90% of Territory, Successfully Seizes Hill 225; Combat Engineer Loses Leg in 9th Landmine Incident

summary: The 2nd Army Region reported that the situation at the Thai-Cambodian border remains tense on December 25-26. Cambodian forces have been using artillery and BM-21 rockets to pressure Thai positions, particularly at Chong Sai Taku in Buriram. Thai forces have responded with proportional artillery fire. Despite the attacks, the military confirms that Thailand maintains full control over all primary strategic areas.
title: ชายแดน ยังตึงเครียดหลายจุด ยิงตอบโต้กันต่อเนื่อง แต่ไทยยังคุมพื้นที่หลักได้ทั้งหมด
titleEn: Border remains tense in many spots, continuous fire exchange, but Thailand still controls all main areas

summary: As of December 26, the third day of General Border Committee (GBC) secretariat talks in Chanthaburi ended without a consensus. Cambodia continues to reject Thailand's three core proposals: a prior formal declaration of ceasefire by Cambodia, a genuine and continuous cessation of fire, and cooperation on demining. The atmosphere is described as very tense, while an ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) from Malaysia continues to monitor the situation.
title: GBC day three: Cambodia still rejects Thai ceasefire terms

summary: Army Region 2 summarized border tension on December 26, noting that Cambodian forces fired BM-21 multiple rocket launchers from the Preah Vihear temple area into Thailand's Phu Ma Khuea. One Thai soldier was injured during artillery exchanges in the Phu Ma Khuea–Don Ao area. Additionally, two soldiers were injured by PMN-2 anti-personnel landmines during clearing operations at Prasat Ta Kwai. Cambodian forces also shelled near Prasat Ta Muen Thom and Chong Sai Taku.
title: ทภ.2 สรุปสถานการณ์ ยังมีปะทะหลายจุด เขมรยิง BM-21 จากเขาพระวิหารใส่ภูมะเขือ ยิงปืนใหญ่เข้าประสาทตาเมือนธม
titleEn: Army Region 2 Summary: Clashes Continue in Multiple Areas; Cambodia Fires BM-21 from Preah Vihear to Phu Ma Khuea

summary: The Government Savings Bank (GSB) has announced special measures to assist those affected by the Thailand-Cambodia border conflict. Debt will be cancelled for soldiers and border patrol police killed in action since December 7, 2025. Additionally, civilians forced to evacuate or who have lost income due to the fighting are eligible for a 3-month debt moratorium with no interest charged.
title: ออมสิน ยกหนี้ทหาร-ตชด. เสียชีวิตเหตุชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา พักหนี้ผู้อพยพที่ขาดรายได้ 3 งวด
titleEn: GSB cancels debt for soldiers killed in border conflict, offers 3-month holiday for affected civilians

summary: The Department of Foreign Trade reported that border trade between Thailand and Cambodia has suffered a loss of approximately 72 billion baht over the first 11 months of 2025. This decline is largely attributed to the persistent border conflict and restricted movement at various checkpoints. Trade with Myanmar is also facing significant challenges due to regional instability.
title: เผยยอด 11 เดือน ค้าชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา เสียหายแล้ว 7.2 หมื่นล้าน
titleEn: 11-month trade figures show 72 billion baht loss in Thai-Cambodian border trade

summary: Thai military units discovered several improvised explosive devices (IEDs) made from RPG heads and C4 explosives in the Ta Kwai area of Surin province. The 2nd Army Area stated this is evidence that Cambodian forces are targeting the lives of personnel moving to assist in the area. Clashes with BM-21 rockets and drones continue in the sector.
title: ทภ.2 พบ “กับระเบิด” แสวงเครื่องอานุภาพทำลายสูงในพื้นที่ตาควาย
titleEn: Army Region 2 Finds High-Explosive IEDs in Ta Kwai Area

summary: A detailed report from Thai Rath describes the escalation of fighting in Sa Kaeo on December 26, just one day before the planned ceasefire. Surapha Task Force soldiers moved to secure 3 strategic points, resulting in a fierce battle. Cambodia reportedly used BM-21 rockets and heavy artillery. The report emphasizes the sacrifice of 3 Thai soldiers and the skepticism regarding Cambodia's sincerity despite their proposal of the '6th draft' at the GBC talks.
title: ตึงเครียดตลอดแนวรบ ก่อนเจรจา “หยุดยิง 72 ชั่วโมง” หวังเริ่มต้น 27 ธ.ค.68
titleEn: Tension Across the Frontline Before '72-Hour Ceasefire' Negotiations Hoped to Start Dec 27, 2025

summary: Secretarial-level talks for the Thailand–Cambodia General Border Committee (GBC) concluded in Chanthaburi on December 26. The two sides have reached a '6th draft' agreement which is now being reviewed by the Thai National Security Council (NSC). If approved, a formal signing ceremony between Thai Defense Minister Gen Natthaphon Narkphanit and Cambodian Defense Minister Gen Tea Seiha is expected on December 27, aimed at initiating a 72-hour ceasefire.
title: GBC talks conclude with 6th draft; NSC decision key to Dec 27 ceasefire

summary: The First Army Region reported that three Thai soldiers from the 2nd Infantry Regiment, 2nd Infantry Battalion, were killed on the evening of December 26 during a Cambodian BM-21 rocket attack at Ban Nong Chan, Khok Sung District, Sa Kaeo province. The deceased were identified as Sgt. Maj. 1st Class Pongsakorn Nakthongdee, Pvt. Patipat Sornpradit, and Pvt. Thiwatawan Phonyiam. The military continues to hold three key positions despite the attacks.
title: ทหารไทยพลีชีพ 3 นายปกป้องอธิปไตยชายแดนบ้านหนองจาน สระแก้ว
titleEn: 3 Thai soldiers killed defending sovereignty at Ban Nong Chan border, Sa Kaeo

summary: Army Region 1 reported that 3 Thai soldiers were killed on December 26 during a strategic operation to secure territory in Sa Kaeo province. The fallen soldiers were identified as Sergeant First Class Pongsakorn Nakthongdee, Private Patiphat Sornpradit, and Private Tiwtawan Phonyiam. Fighting was most intense at Ban Nong Chan, where Cambodian forces used heavy artillery. Currently, 18,188 Thai civilians are taking refuge in 40 temporary shelters across four districts in Sa Kaeo.
title: ด่วน! ทหารเสียชีวิต สมรภูมิบ้านหนองจาน 3 นาย หลังดำเนินกลยุทธ์ เพื่อยึดครอง 3 พื้นที่ จ.สระแก้ว
titleEn: Urgent! 3 Soldiers Killed in Ban Nong Chan Battlefield After Operation to Secure 3 Areas in Sa Kaeo

summary: An urgent request for clear passage on Mittraphap and Phahonyothin roads was issued for ambulances transporting three soldiers injured in border clashes in Surin province. The soldiers are being moved to Phramongkutklao Hospital in Bangkok, which has the highest capability for treating war-related injuries.
title: ขอทางด่วน ส่ง 3 ทหารกล้าเหยื่อปะทะชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา เข้ากรุงเทพฯ
titleEn: Expressway requested for ambulance moving 3 brave soldiers from border clashes to Bangkok

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul confirmed that the National Security Council has authorized the Defense Minister to sign a ceasefire agreement in Chanthaburi on Saturday. However, hostilities continued late Friday as a Cambodian rocket attack in Surin province killed three Thai soldiers and injured 17 others. Anutin emphasized that while Thailand agrees to the truce, it will not accept returning to pre-conflict positions in secured areas, stating Thailand 'cannot retreat'.
title: Hopes rise for ceasefire
titleEn: Hopes rise for ceasefire despite late Friday casualties

summary: Authorities in Ubon Ratchathani, Surin, and Sa Kaeo have issued urgent warnings for residents to remain in bunkers or evacuation centers until a projected ceasefire at 12:00 PM on Saturday, Dec 27. Officials fear that Cambodian forces may launch heavy attacks or long-range artillery strikes in the final hours leading up to the truce in an attempt to regain lost strategic positions. Local defense volunteers have been told to dim lights and watch for unidentified drones.
title: Border districts urge residents to stay in bunkers ahead of expected noon ceasefire on December 27

summary: Following the GBC Joint Statement, the Thai military (Army Regions 1 and 2) reported successful reclamation and control of key strategic border areas. In Sa Kaeo, Thai forces secured Ban Khlong Phaeng, Ban Nong Chan, and Ban Nong Ya Kaeo. In Surin and Sisaket, troops established control over Hill 225 and areas near Preah Vihear before the 12:00 PM ceasefire took effect on Dec 27. The 72-hour window is now being used to verify sincerity before the potential return of 18 captured Cambodian soldiers.
title: เช็กพื้นที่ล่าสุด ไทยยึดคืนได้ หลังเจรจาหยุดยิง 72 ชั่วโมง
titleEn: Checking Latest Areas Reclaimed by Thailand After 72-Hour Ceasefire Negotiation

summary: The Election Commission (EC) of Thailand has published special guidelines in the Royal Gazette to ensure the upcoming general election can proceed in Chanthaburi, Trat, Buri Ram, Si Sa Ket, Sa Kaeo, Surin, and Ubon Ratchathani. Due to the border conflict and evacuations, officials are authorized to use electronic systems for voter list notifications if physical delivery is unsafe, and to adapt polling procedures to prioritize voter safety without disenfranchising citizens in conflict zones.
title: Election safeguards extend to border areas
titleEn: Election Commission issues special voting measures for 7 border provinces

summary: Thai and Cambodian General Border Committee (GBC) secretariats have finalized a draft ceasefire agreement after three days of tense negotiations in Chanthaburi. The deal, which includes a 72-hour halt to hostilities, is scheduled for signing by the defense ministers of both nations on Saturday, Dec 27. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul stated that Thailand will not trade territory for business interests and that the military has successfully established sovereignty over contested areas.
title: เจรจา GBC ไทย-เขมรจบแล้ว หยุดยิง 72 ชม. กห. 2 ฝ่ายลงนาม 27 ธ.ค.
titleEn: GBC talks concluded: 72-hour ceasefire agreed, Defense Ministers to sign Dec 27

summary: The Second Army Region of Thailand reports that it has successfully gained 100% control over the Ban Nong Chan area. Troops are currently fortifying positions at Phu Ma Khua and Ta Kwai due to a high risk of Cambodian forces attempting to retake lost ground. The report notes recent heavy clashes involving Cambodian BM-21 rocket launchers striking civilian areas and confirmed that Thai F-16s conducted airstrikes against Cambodian weapon depots in Siem Reap province, more than 60km from the border.
title: ยึดหนองจาน100% ทภ.2ตรึงกำลังภูมะเขือ-ตาควาย เสี่ยงสูงกัมพูชาจ้องโจมตีเอาคืน
titleEn: Ban Nong Chan 100% secured; Army Region 2 on high alert at Phu Ma Khua and Ta Kwai for potential counter-attacks

summary: As of the morning of December 27, the 2nd Army Area reported that the situation along the Northeastern border remains tense. Clashes involving heavy weaponry continued through December 26 in Si Sa Ket province. Thai forces maintain control of strategic high grounds despite constant pressure.
title: ในประเทศ - ทภ 2 สรุปสถานการณ์ชายแดนไทยกัมพูชา ศรีสะเกษปะทะหนัก หลายพื้นที่ยังตึงเครียด
titleEn: Army Region 2 Summary: Heavy Clashes in Si Sa Ket, Tensions Remain High

summary: The 1st Army Area released a tribute to three soldiers (one Master Sergeant and two Privates) who were killed on December 26 while defending Ban Nong Chan in Sa Kaeo. Cambodian forces reportedly used heavy artillery and mortars to attack the position after Thai troops successfully secured the area.
title: กองทัพภาคที่ 1 สดุดีทหารกล้า 3 นาย สังกัด ร.2 พัน.2 รอ. สละชีพปกป้องอธิปไตยของไทย
titleEn: 1st Army Area Honors 3 Fallen Soldiers from 2nd Infantry Regiment

summary: The 1st Army Area clarified that social media reports claiming the death of Private Nithikorn Somtum are false. The soldier was injured in the line of duty at Ban Nong Chan and underwent successful surgery; he is currently in safe condition under medical supervision.
title: ทภ 1 แจ้ง พลทหารนิธิกร ไม่ได้เสียชีวิต แค่ได้รับบาดเจ็บ อยู่ระหว่างแพทย์ดูแลใกล้ชิด
titleEn: Army Confirms Private Nithikorn is Not Dead, Only Injured

summary: Details of the 3rd Special General Border Committee (GBC) meeting report a 16-point agreement. Key points include an immediate ceasefire starting at 12:00 PM on Dec 27 covering all weapons, freezing troop movements/patrols, and allowing civilians to return home. The agreement explicitly states it does not affect border demarcation, which remains the responsibility of the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC).
title: เปิดรายละเอียดไทย-กัมพูชาหยุดยิง 16 ข้อ งดโจมตีทุกประเภท คงทหารไว้ตำแหน่งปัจจุบัน ไม่เกี่ยวเรื่องเขตแดน-โยนกลับเป็นหน้าที่ JBC
titleEn: Full 16-Point Thai-Cambodian Ceasefire Details: End All Attacks, Maintain Current Troop Positions, Border Issues Referred to JBC

summary: Thai and Cambodian defense ministers signed a Joint Statement in Chanthaburi to end hostilities. The deal includes a 72-hour 'danger zone' period to prove sincerity before returning 18 Cambodian POWs. Cooperation on humanitarian demining and cybercrime suppression was also highlighted as urgent agendas to build trust.
title: ไทย-กัมพูชา ลดตึงเครียด-หยุดยิง มีผลเวลา 12.00 น. วันที่ 27 ธ.ค. 68 หลังประชุม GBC
titleEn: Thailand-Cambodia Reduce Tension: Ceasefire Effective 12:00 PM Dec 27, 2025 After GBC Meeting

summary: The Thai military's official news channel reports that the GBC meeting at Ban Pak Kard, Chanthaburi, resulted in a signed Joint Statement. Cambodia agreed to a 72-hour ceasefire in exchange for the return of 18 military prisoners. The ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) was present during the ceremony. The military honors 3 soldiers who died in the recent defense of the border.
title: ลงนามแล้ว! GBC ไทย-กัมพูชาหยุดยิง 72 ชม. - สถานีวิทยุโทรทัศน์กองทัพบก
titleEn: Signed! Thai-Cambodian GBC Ceasefire for 72 Hours - Royal Thai Army Radio and Television

summary: Defense Minister Gen. Natthaphon Narkphanit announced that the GBC meeting resulted in a Joint Statement. Both sides agreed to stop firing from 12:00 PM on December 27. Troops will remain at current positions with no reinforcements or provocations. A 72-hour monitoring period will confirm the ceasefire's sincerity before 18 captured Cambodian soldiers are released. Malaysian Prime Minister also welcomed the move.
title: ไทย-กัมพูชา: จับมือสงบศึก! ลงนามหยุดยิงตั้งแต่เที่ยงวันนี้ สังเกตการณ์ต่อ 72 ชม.
titleEn: Thailand-Cambodia: Truce reached! Ceasefire signed effective noon today with 72-hour monitoring

summary: Army Region 2 reported border incidents occurring before the noon ceasefire on Dec 27. At Khao Satta Som in Si Sa Ket, Private Narin Ngaoprai was seriously injured (lost a leg) after stepping on a PMN-2 landmine during a clearing operation. Two other soldiers, Sgt. Maj. Sirasak Jitboon and Sgt. (unnamed), sustained gunshot wounds during a clash. The military claimed they were clearing Cambodian trenches on the western side of the mountain.
title: เกาะติดชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชาวันนี้ ทหารไทยเหยียบทุ่นระเบิด 1 ราย ถูกยิง 2 ราย
titleEn: Border watch today: One Thai soldier hits landmine, two shot

summary: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) released a statement acknowledging the latest development at the border. Thailand and Cambodia reached a joint agreement during the Special General Border Committee (GBC) Meeting 3/2025 held at the Ban Phak Kat permanent crossing in Chanthaburi. The ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) was present to witness the agreement, which aims to de-escalate the conflict.
title: กต.แถลงการณ์รับทราบไทย กัมพูชา บรรลุข้อตกลงหยุดยิง เที่ยงวันนี้
titleEn: MFA statement acknowledges Thailand-Cambodia ceasefire agreement effective noon today

summary: Air Chief Marshal Prapas Sornchaidee, director of the joint border situation news center, stated that following the ceasefire agreement at noon on Dec 27, there will be a 72-hour monitoring period. He emphasized that if Cambodia does not remain peaceful during this time, the Thai military is 100% prepared to resume defensive measures. He also mentioned that the 18 Cambodian soldiers would be returned only after this 72-hour period is successfully maintained.
title: ผอ.ศูนย์แถลงข่าวร่วมฯ ลั่น ถ้า 72 ชม. กัมพูชายังไม่นิ่งไทยจะใช้มาตรการเดิมปกป้องตนเอง
titleEn: Director of Joint News Center Warns: If Cambodia Is Not Quiet Within 72 Hours, Thailand Will Resume Self-Defense Measures

summary: Thailand and Cambodia signed a 16-point Joint Statement during the General Border Committee (GBC) meeting, effective Dec 27, 2025, at 12:00 PM. The agreement mandates an immediate halt to all weapon use and troop movements. Both sides must maintain current positions without advancement or provocation. A 72-hour monitoring period is established to verify compliance. Following this period, Thailand will return 18 captured Cambodian soldiers.
title: ไทย-กัมพูชาลงนามหยุดยิง ตั้งแต่ 12.00 น.วันนี้ เปิดถ้อยแถลง 16 ข้อ
titleEn: Thailand-Cambodia sign ceasefire starting 12:00 PM today, 16-point statement revealed

summary: The General Border Committee (GBC) released a 16-point joint statement signed by the defense ministers of Thailand and Cambodia. Key measures include an immediate ceasefire effective Dec 27 at noon, a ban on moving additional troops or provocative actions, and a commitment to humanitarian landmine clearance. The agreement also includes a clause to refrain from disseminating fake news about the conflict.
title: เปิดถ้อยแถลง ไทย-กัมพูชา หยุดยิงทันที 12.00 น. วันนี้ ไม่เคลื่อนย้ายกำลัง-ยั่วยุเพิ่มตึงเครียด
titleEn: Full Statement: Thailand-Cambodia Immediate Ceasefire at 12:00 PM Today

summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi has invited Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow to Yunnan, China, on December 28-29. The visit aims to facilitate a trilateral meeting between China, Thailand, and Cambodia to build upon the Special GBC results and support a sustainable ceasefire and long-term peace.
title: ‘หวัง อี้’ เชิญ ‘สีหศักดิ์’ เยือนจีน 28-29 ธ.ค. ถก 3 ฝ่ายสางปัญหาไทย-กัมพูชา
titleEn: Wang Yi invites Sihasak to China Dec 28-29 for trilateral talks to resolve Thai-Cambodian conflict

summary: The Thai military's Joint Press Centre stated that Thailand has secured key terrain within sovereign areas and achieved military objectives. The 72-hour ceasefire is described as a 'test of sincerity' rather than a permanent peace. If firing occurs, Thai forces will respond under rules of engagement. Just before the noon deadline, one Thai soldier was reported severely injured by a newly planted landmine.
title: Military says objectives achieved; 72-hour ceasefire is “not the end”

summary: The First Army Region Operations Center reported that after checking the frontlines at Ban Khlong Phaeng, Ban Nong Ya Kaeo, and Ban Nong Chan in Sa Kaeo, both sides have ceased military operations. This follows the GBC agreement signed in Chanthaburi. Border residents are advised to wait for official announcements before returning home.
title: ทภ.1อัพเดท ชายแดนไทยกัมพูชา จ. สระแก้ว หยุดยิงแล้ว
titleEn: First Army Region updates: Thailand-Cambodia border in Sa Kaeo has ceased firing

summary: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) acknowledged the ceasefire agreement reached at the 3rd Special GBC meeting held at Ban Phakkad, Chanthaburi. Thailand set three clear conditions for the truce: 1) Official and sincere declaration, 2) Actual and continuous cessation of fighting, and 3) Sincerity in resolving landmine issues. The MFA expressed condolences for the brave Thai soldiers who sacrificed their lives protecting sovereignty. The 72-hour observation window will determine if civilians can safely return home.
title: กต.ออกแถลงการณ์ผล GBC สมัยพิเศษ ไทย-กัมพูชาลงนาม หยุดยิงแล้ว
titleEn: MFA issues statement on Special GBC results: Thailand-Cambodia sign ceasefire

summary: The First Army Region reported that operations in Sa Kaeo province (Ta Phraya and Khok Sung districts) have ceased following the Joint Statement. While soldiers remain in their positions to defend sovereignty, no further clashes were reported in these areas after the midday deadline. Civilians are advised to wait for official government clearance before returning home.
title: ทภ.1 สรุปสถานการณ์ชายแดน 3 พื้นที่ หยุดปฏิบัติการทางทหาร ยึดกรอบ GBC ไทย–กัมพูชา
titleEn: Army Region 1 summarizes border situation in 3 areas, halts military operations following GBC framework

summary: The Thai Mine Action Centre (TMAC) has condemned Cambodia for laying fresh PMN-2 landmines along the border in Si Sa Ket province. This follows an incident where a Thai soldier lost his leg. TMAC claims to have found evidence, including a GPS notepad left by retreating Cambodian forces, indicating the mines were recently placed, violating the Ottawa Convention.
title: Thai agency accuses Cambodian forces of planting new landmines

summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio released a statement through the US Embassy in Bangkok welcoming the ceasefire between Thailand and Cambodia following the GBC meeting. He urged both nations to strictly adhere to the 'Kuala Lumpur Peace Accords.' Meanwhile, Thai Caretaker PM Anutin Charnvirakul is scheduled to visit Buriram to oversee the safe return of displaced villagers to their homes following the cessation of hostilities.
title: สหรัฐฯ หนุนหยุดยิง! "มาร์โค รูบิโอ" ยินดีไทย-กัมพูชา บรรลุข้อตกลงสันติภาพ
titleEn: US Supports Ceasefire! Marco Rubio Welcomes Thai-Cambodia Peace Agreement

summary: Prime Minister and Interior Minister Anutin Charnvirakul is traveling to Buriram to oversee the return of displaced persons from shelters to their homes. This follows the 72-hour ceasefire window established during GBC talks. Anutin noted the situation is improving but remained skeptical of reports regarding Belarusian transport planes landing in Phnom Penh, stating security agencies are monitoring the situation closely.
title: อนุทินเตรียมบินบุรีรัมย์ ส่งผู้อพยพกลับบ้านหลังหยุดยิงไทย–กัมพูชา
titleEn: Anutin prepares to fly to Buriram to send evacuees home after Thai-Cambodia ceasefire

summary: Air Chief Marshal Prapas Sornjaidee, spokesperson for the joint situation center, stated that the military remains on high alert. He clarified that the areas currently held by Thai troops are considered Thai territory, specifically mentioning Ban Nong Chan. Cambodian civilians are prohibited from entering these zones. The army is prepared to respond immediately to any provocation or violation of the Joint Statement.
title: กองทัพ ยัน ไทยไม่ประมาท พร้อมตอบโต้หากเขมรละเมิดหยุดยิง ย้ำ บ้านหนองจานเป็นเขตไทย
titleEn: Army insists Thailand is not complacent, ready to retaliate if Cambodia violates ceasefire, emphasizes Ban Nong Chan is Thai territory

summary: The Second Army Region has officially announced that the border situation has stabilized following the ceasefire agreement. Authorities are now allowing displaced Thai civilians to return to their homes and villages. However, the military emphasizes that residents should remain cautious and follow official safety instructions as troops continue to monitor the area to ensure sovereignty and public safety.
title: สถานการณ์สงบแล้ว! กองทัพภาคที่ 2 เปิดทางประชาชนกลับบ้านตามปกติ
titleEn: Situation Calmed! Army Region 2 Allows Citizens to Return Home as Normal

summary: Acting PM Anutin Charnvirakul discussed the outcome of the GBC meeting, stating the Joint Statement clearly binds both nations to cease hostilities. He addressed rumors of a Belarusian cargo plane potentially carrying weapons to Phnom Penh, noting that military intelligence is monitoring the situation. He expressed hope that Cambodia would honor the agreement this time, especially with China's invitation for further peace talks in Kunming on Dec 28-29.
title: 'อนุทิน' ระบุ Joint Statement รมว.กลาโหม ไทย-กัมพูชา ชัดเจน 2 ฝ่ายจะไม่ละเมิดกันและกันอีก
titleEn: Anutin states Joint Statement between Thai-Cambodian Defense Ministers is clear: both sides will not violate each other again

summary: Reports from Cambodia's Customs Department show a 35% decrease in imports from Thailand between June and November 2025 due to border tensions and the closure of key trade checkpoints like Sai Taku and Chong Jom. Bilateral trade has slowed significantly, and there are currently no signs of economic recovery despite the recent ceasefire agreement.
title: ต่างประเทศ - ปิดด่านชายแดนพ่นพิษ กัมพูชาเผยยอดนำเข้าจากไทยวูบ ยังไม่มีสัญญาณฟื้นตัว
titleEn: Foreign News - Border closures take toll: Cambodia reports plunge in Thai imports with no recovery signs

summary: Army Region 2 reported that overall tensions have eased following the midday ceasefire on December 27. While morning clashes involving rockets and artillery occurred in Ubon Ratchathani and Sisaket provinces, the situation stabilized afterward. Thai forces continue to occupy regained territories. Surveillance remains tight in areas like Preah Vihear and nearby hills where movements were still detected post-truce.
title: สรุปสถานการณ์ชายแดนไทย–กัมพูชา กองทัพภาคที่ 2 เผยหลังหยุดยิงความรุนแรงลดลงชัดเจน
titleEn: Summary of Thai-Cambodia border situation: Army Region 2 says violence significantly decreased after ceasefire

summary: The Chinese Foreign Ministry expressed support for the ceasefire agreement signed by Thailand and Cambodia. China is hosting a trilateral meeting in Yunnan from December 28-29 to further strengthen the ceasefire and restore political trust and normal relations between the two neighbors. The US has also welcomed the deal, urging both nations to follow through immediately.
title: โฆษกกต. "จีน" ยินดีไทย-กัมพูชา ลงนามหยุดยิง ส่งสัญญาณพร้อมมีบทบาท สร้างสันติภาพร่วม 2 ประเทศ
titleEn: Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson welcomes Thai-Cambodian ceasefire, signaling readiness to play a role in peace

summary: The 2nd Army Region issued an official announcement stating that the border conflict has eased following the ceasefire agreement. Citizens who were evacuated are now permitted to return to their homes and normal residences, though they are advised to remain cautious about safety. The military remains in the area to protect sovereignty and public property.
title: กองทัพภาคที่ 2 ประกาศให้ประชาชน กลับที่พัก ภูมิลำเนาได้แล้ว
titleEn: 2nd Army Region announces residents can return to their homes

summary: ACM Prapas Sonjaidee, director of Thailand's Joint Press Centre, stated that Thailand now expects diplomatic forums to resolve differences instead of the battlefield. While the truce is holding and evacuees are returning, the Thai Air Force monitored a Russian-built IL-62 aircraft from Belarus landing in Phnom Penh. Thailand maintains its right to self-defense and retaliation if weapons are used again, while documenting evidence for international organizations.
title: Thailand expects diplomacy to replace fighting with Cambodia

summary: Caretaker PM Anutin Charnvirakul disclosed that China has offered 20 million yuan (approx. 95 million THB) in aid to both Thailand and Cambodia for post-conflict reconstruction. Anutin visited border provinces including Buriram and Surin to oversee the return of displaced persons. He noted that while social media questioned China's neutrality, the offer was extended to both nations. He also visited strategic sites like Prasat Ta Kwai to boost morale.
title: 'อนุทิน' เผย 'ไทย-กัมพูชา' ได้รับข้อเสนอ 20 ล้านหยวน จากจีน ฟื้นฟูหลังสงคราม
titleEn: Anutin Reveals China Offers 20 Million Yuan to Thailand and Cambodia for Recovery

summary: The Thai military continues to maintain a 24-hour presence along the Cambodian border to guard against potential ceasefire violations. A Thai soldier was reported injured by a landmine while clearing an area. The military emphasizes that the ceasefire does not mean a reduction in territorial defense or sovereignty protection.
title: ‘กองทัพ’ ตรึงกำลังชายแดนกัมพูชา24ชม. หวั่น ละเมิดหยุดยิง
titleEn: Military Maintains 24-Hour Border Presence, Fearing Ceasefire Violations

summary: Bilateral trade between Thailand and Cambodia has taken a severe hit due to border tensions. Data from Cambodia's Customs Department shows a 34.5% decrease in imports from Thailand in the second half of 2025, falling from $1.77 billion to $1.25 billion. The drop is attributed to the closure of key border crossings like Sai Taku and Chong Jom during the height of the conflict.
title: กัมพูชาเผยยอดนำเข้าจากไทย ลดลง 34.5% ระหว่างมิ.ย.-พ.ย. ปีนี้
titleEn: Cambodia reveals imports from Thailand dropped 34.5% between June-Nov this year

summary: Defense Minister Nattaphon Narkphanit emphasized that the ceasefire is a strategic move to verify Cambodia's commitment to peace, not a sign of surrender. He stated that Thailand maintains the right to self-defense if the truce is violated and that the 72-hour observation period is essential for verification. He also noted that Thai forces have regained control of key strategic areas.
title: Ceasefire agreement 'not a retreat'

summary: The Thailand Mine Action Centre (TMAC) discovered PMN-2 anti-personnel landmines at abandoned Cambodian bases in Si Sa Ket, along with logs of mine-laying operations. A Thai soldier lost a leg after stepping on a mine shortly after the ceasefire began. Additionally, BM-21 rocket remnants were found in Buriram farmlands. TMAC urged Cambodia to disclose mine locations to ensure safety.
title: TMAC finds mines, rockets, after pact

summary: Caretaker PM Anutin Charnvirakul visited Buriram, Surin, and Amnat Charoen to monitor the border situation. He stated the 72-hour ceasefire expires tomorrow (Dec 30) at noon. He confirmed no reports of unauthorized drones and mentioned China's proposal of 20 million yuan in aid for damage, which Thailand is currently considering.
title: ไทย-กัมพูชา: "อนุทิน" ลงพื้นที่ 3 จ.ชายแดนอีสานใต้ ก่อนครบกำหนดหยุดยิงพรุ่งนี้ ไร้เงาโดรนป่วน
titleEn: Thailand-Cambodia: 'Anutin' Visits 3 Southern Border Provinces Before Ceasefire Expires Tomorrow; No Signs of Disruptive Drones

summary: The Ministry of Public Health reported that Kantharalak Hospital has reopened, though 6 other border hospitals remain closed. One patient injured on Dec 27 passed away, bringing the death toll up. Around 80,000 people remain in 660 shelters, with mental health teams monitoring high-stress levels among evacuees.
title: สธ.เผยสถานการณ์ไทย-กัมพูชาเริ่มคลี่คลาย รพ.กันทรลักษ์ กลับมาเปิดบริการตามปกติ
titleEn: Public Health Ministry Says Thailand-Cambodia Situation Easing; Kantharalak Hospital Resumes Normal Service

summary: Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow met with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Cambodian FM Prak Sokhonn in Yunnan. China emphasized its non-interference policy but aims to facilitate a platform for sustainable peace. Thailand reaffirmed its path towards peace, focusing on building trust, reducing confrontation, and demining to return safety to civilians.
title: ไทย–กัมพูชา เปิดโต๊ะสามฝ่าย จีนหนุนบทบาทสันติภาพ หลังข้อตกลงหยุดยิงชายแดน
titleEn: Thailand-Cambodia Open Tripartite Talks, China Supports Peace Role After Border Ceasefire

summary: Thai PBS reports on the political framing of the ceasefire. Cambodian PM Hun Manet posted on Facebook clarifying that the ceasefire is not a surrender or a loss of territory, but a choice for the safety of the people. He noted that 32 civilians have died and 93 have been injured in the recent 20-day conflict. Meanwhile, Thai security sources noted that Cambodia requested to let its people return to certain disputed areas (Nong Chan and Nong Ya Kaeo), but Thailand ignored the request.
title: “ฮุน เซน” อกแตก “ไทย-เขมร” หยุดยิง “สร้างสันติภาพ” บนเส้นทางคู่ขนาน
titleEn: Hun Sen Distraught? Thai-Khmer Ceasefire to Build Peace on Parallel Paths

summary: Cambodian PM Hun Manet posted on Facebook clarifying that the 'Stand-still Ceasefire' effective since Dec 27 is for protecting civilian lives, not due to military weakness or territorial concessions. He reported 32 Cambodian civilian deaths and 500,000 displaced. He also noted that Thailand is scheduled to release 18 captured Cambodian soldiers today (Dec 30) following the 72-hour period.
title: "ฮุน มาเนต" ย้ำหยุดยิงไม่ใช่การ "พ่ายแพ้" หรือ "แลกดินแดน" ยันอธิปไตยยังคงเดิมจ่อรับ 18 ทหารกลับบ้าน
titleEn: Hun Manet insists ceasefire is not 'defeat' or 'land swap,' sovereignty remains intact; prepares to receive 18 soldiers

summary: The Thai Army Spokesperson team reported on social media that over 250 drones from Cambodia have crossed into Thai territory, which is considered a violation of the GBC de-escalation measures. The news has sparked significant concern and reactions from Thai citizens online.
title: ในประเทศ - โดรนกัมพูชา ล้ำ อธิปไตยไทย มากกว่า 250 ลำ
titleEn: Domestic: Over 250 Cambodian Drones Violate Thai Sovereignty

summary: Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow stated that trilateral talks in Yunnan with China and Cambodia met Thailand's expectations. He clarified that China acted as a facilitator and that Thailand maintains that the dispute must be resolved bilaterally. The immediate priority is a sustainable ceasefire and sincerity in adhering to the terms, followed by landmine clearance.
title: Three-way meeting produces 'positive results'

summary: True Corporation is coordinating with the Royal Thai Armed Forces and the NBTC to repair communication infrastructure damaged during the border conflict. The company is following signal control policies in border areas to support national security missions while ensuring residents can communicate as the situation stabilizes following the ceasefire agreement.
title: ทรู คอร์ปอเรชั่น เร่งลงพื้นที่ชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชาติดตามความเสียหายและกู้สัญญาณมือถือต่อเนื่อง
titleEn: True Corporation Rushes to Thai-Cambodia Border to Monitor Damage and Restore Mobile Signals

summary: Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow met with Cambodian FM Prak Sokhonn and Chinese FM Wang Yi in Yunnan. China emphasized it respects the principle of non-interference but wishes to facilitate a channel for both countries to discuss lasting peace. Thailand reaffirmed its desire to progress relations step-by-step post-ceasefire and will consider repatriating 18 Cambodian soldiers after the 72-hour ceasefire holds. Both sides agreed to discuss landmine clearance and anti-scam operations.
title: ไทย-กัมพูชา เปิดโต๊ะสามฝ่าย จีนย้ำไม่แทรกแซง หนุนบทบาทสันติภาพ
titleEn: Thailand-Cambodia Trilateral Meeting: China Stresses Non-Interference, Supports Peace Role

summary: The Royal Thai Army (RTA) announced on December 29 that it detected over 250 Cambodian unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) violating Thai sovereignty. This activity is considered a breach of the GBC de-escalation agreement. As a result, the RTA is reconsidering the release of 18 Cambodian soldiers who were to be repatriated after a successful 72-hour ceasefire. The Army emphasized its duty to protect national interests while remaining committed to peace mechanisms.
title: ทบ. พบ UAV กัมพูชาล้ำชายแดน 250 ลำ ทบทวนปล่อย 18 เชลย
titleEn: Army Finds 250 Cambodian UAVs Crossing Border, Reviews Release of 18 Prisoners

summary: Cambodian Deputy PM Prak Sokhonn stated that if conditions remain stable, 18 Cambodian soldiers held by Thailand since July 2025 are expected to be released at 12:00 PM on December 30. The release follows the 72-hour ceasefire agreement period. Thailand has reportedly notified the International Red Cross to coordinate the process.
title: รองนายกฯกัมพูชารอลุ้น คาด 18 ทหารเชลยศึกจะถูกปล่อยตัวพรุ่งนี้ ลั่นจะไม่มีปัญหาใดๆ
titleEn: Cambodian DPM Expects Release of 18 Prisoners of War Tomorrow, Vows No Issues

summary: The Thai Army reported detecting numerous Cambodian drones violating Thai airspace, totaling over 250 incursions. Consequently, the planned release of 18 Cambodian prisoners of war, originally scheduled for noon on December 30 after a 72-hour ceasefire, has been postponed. The Thai military views these drone activities as a violation of the de-escalation measures agreed upon during the recent GBC meeting.
title: ทบ.พบโดรนเขมรรุกล้ำอธิปไตย เลื่อนส่งคืน 18 เชลย
titleEn: Thai Army Finds Cambodian Drones Violating Sovereignty, Postpones Return of 18 Prisoners

summary: Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata, spokesperson for the Cambodian Ministry of National Defense, issued a statement on December 29 categorically denying Thai claims that 250 drones flew from Cambodia into Thai territory. She emphasized that Cambodia remains committed to the General Border Committee (GBC) joint statement from December 27 and has strict orders prohibiting any UAV launches in border areas.
title: ‘มาลี’ โต้ไทย เขมรยึดมั่นในสันติภาพ ไม่ได้ส่งโดรนกว่า 250 ลำล้ำแดน
titleEn: Maly Rebuts Thailand: Cambodia Committed to Peace, Denies Sending 250 Drones Across Border

summary: Border Patrol Police and Humanitarian Mine Action Unit 1 are inspecting and disposing of unexploded ordnance, including BM-21 rocket remnants and artillery shells, in border villages of Sa Kaeo Province. Residents returning home are warned not to touch suspicious objects and to report them to authorities immediately via hotlines 191 or 1599.
title: Thai authorities clear unexploded ordnance along Thailand–Cambodia border to ensure civilian safety

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of National Defence has categorically rejected claims made by the Thai side on Dec 29 that over 250 drones flew from Cambodia into Thai territory. A spokesperson stated that strict orders are in place prohibiting the launch of any UAVs and reaffirmed Cambodia's commitment to the Dec 27 ceasefire agreement.
title: เขมรปฏิเสธข้อกล่าวหาไทย โดรน 250 ลำรุกล้ำน่านฟ้า
titleEn: Cambodia denies Thai allegations of 250 drones violating airspace

summary: In the wake of a brokered ceasefire, China hosted trilateral talks in Yunnan province on December 29. While Beijing positions itself as a peacemaker, tension remains as the Thai army reports drone violations by Cambodia. Thailand is reportedly 'reconsidering' the planned release of 18 Cambodian prisoners due to these fresh violations of the ceasefire agreement.
title: China steps out of diplomatic shadows to take credit for efforts on Cambodia-Thailand ceasefire

summary: Local reporters in Surin noted that residents who returned home during the 72-hour ceasefire (expiring noon, Dec 30) are on high alert. Cambodian sources claimed their military has not allowed Cambodian civilians back into the O'Smach area, contrasting with Thai authorities allowing Thais to return. Vendors at Chong Chom market expressed a lack of trust in the ceasefire and readiness to flee immediately if fighting erupts.
title: ลุ้นเที่ยงนี้! ครบ 72 ชม. ไทย-กัมพูชา ลงนามหยุดยิง แม่ค้าชายแดนช่องจอมไม่กลัว พร้อมอพยพทุกเมื่อ
titleEn: Tension at noon! 72-hour ceasefire ends; Chong Chom border vendors ready to evacuate if war resumes

summary: Army Region 2 reported the border situation as of Dec 29, noting no heavy weapon clashes during the 72-hour ceasefire. However, they detected Cambodian military movements, including about 30 trucks transporting logistics from Ban Char to Ban Kon Prambei in Ubon Ratchathani and Sisaket, and drones patrolling Thai positions.
title: นับถอยหลังหยุดยิงครบ 72 ชม. ทภ.2 แจ้งยังไร้เหตุปะทะชายแดนกัมพูชา
titleEn: Countdown to end of 72-hour ceasefire; Army Region 2 reports no clashes on Cambodian border

summary: The Ministry of Interior held a meeting on Dec 29 with governors from 7 border provinces to coordinate the implementation of the GBC joint statement. Officials emphasized monitoring the 72-hour ceasefire expiration at noon on Dec 30 and ensuring the safety of civilians returning home, under the 'Safe and Dignified' return principle.
title: ก.มหาดไทย ประชุมผู้ว่าฯ ชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา ถกเข้มแนวทางปฏิบัติข้อตกลง GBC
titleEn: Interior Ministry meets border governors to discuss GBC agreement implementation

summary: Caretaker Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul stated that the 72-hour ceasefire observation period officially ends at 12:00 PM today (Dec 30). Security agencies report the situation is normal, but the PM warned that the military cannot yet be fully complacent. He emphasized the need for continued vigilance despite the current lack of clashes.
title: ชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชายังสงบ "อนุทิน" จับตาครบ 72 ชม. หยุดยิง 12.00 น. วันนี้
titleEn: Thai-Cambodia border remains calm; Anutin monitors completion of 72-hour ceasefire at noon today

summary: Thailand has officially postponed the scheduled release of 18 Cambodian soldiers (originally set for Dec 30) after security agencies detected Cambodian drones violating Thai airspace. This action is considered a breach of the GBC joint statement which prohibits provocations. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Nikorndej Balankura stated the landmine incidents are also a serious concern for the Thai side.
title: สีหศักดิ์แจงคณะทูต ไทยเลื่อนปล่อย 18 ทหารกัมพูชา หลังพบโดรนรุกล้ำ
titleEn: Sihasak briefs diplomats: Thailand postpones release of 18 Cambodian troops due to drone violations

summary: The Thai Cabinet acknowledged the Ministry of Commerce's measures to help citizens and businesses affected by the border conflict. Key actions include controlling commodity prices, finding new markets for exporters, and providing free space for small vendors and OTOP producers to sell products outside the conflict zones.
title: ครม.รับทราบมาตรการบรรเทาผลกระทบชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา
titleEn: Cabinet acknowledges measures to mitigate impact on Thai-Cambodian border

summary: The National Mine Action Center (NMAC) reported that on Dec 29, a Thai soldier from the 1st Cavalry Division lost his left leg and suffered eye injuries after stepping on a landmine while clearing an area in Kantharalak, Sisaket. This is the 11th Thai soldier to suffer such a loss since the conflict began. NMAC condemned the use of mines as a violation of the Ottawa Convention.
title: ศทช.แถลงทุ่นระเบิดสังหารเขมร ทําทหารไทยสูญเสียรายที่ 11 ภัยเงียบละเมิดออตตาวา
titleEn: NMAC announces Cambodian landmine claims 11th Thai soldier casualty, calling it a violation of Ottawa Treaty

summary: Thai PBS summarizes the Army Region 2 report, highlighting specific drone incursions near Prasat Ta Muen Thom (31 drones) and sightings of Cambodian patrols. While heavy artillery has ceased, the military suspects these movements are for assessing Thai deployments. Residents are urged to report suspicious objects to EOD teams.
title: ทภ.2 ยันชายแดนไร้ปะทะ พบกัมพูชาขนกำลัง-โดรนสอดแนม
titleEn: Army Region 2: Border quiet but Cambodian troop movement and drones detected

summary: The Thai Border Joint Situation News Center announced response plans for potential violations after the ceasefire expired at noon. Thailand has established a 'Red Line' (prohibiting sovereignty violation, civilian attacks, or threats). Responses will be proportionate to the level of provocation. Decisions on the 18 prisoners depend on humanitarian and safety assessments.
title: ไทย-กัมพูชา: วัดใจกัมพูชาหลังครบ 72 ชม.หยุดยิง ไทยยกระดับเฝ้าระวัง-เตือนภัยเชิงรุก
titleEn: Thai-Cambodia: Testing Cambodia's sincerity after 72-hour ceasefire; Thailand elevates proactive surveillance

summary: Lt. Gen. Weerayut Raksilp, Commander of the 2nd Army Area, visited 19 soldiers currently hospitalized in Surin for injuries sustained during recent border clashes. He assured the troops and their families that the army would provide full medical care and welfare benefits throughout the New Year period.
title: 'แม่ทัพเติ่ง' เยี่ยม 19 ทหารบาดเจ็บเหตุปะทะชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา
titleEn: Army Region 2 Commander visits 19 soldiers injured in Thai-Cambodian border clashes

summary: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs officially confirmed the repatriation of 18 Cambodian soldiers who had been held since July 2025. The release occurred at 10:00 AM on December 31, 2025, following a 72-hour ceasefire. The ministry emphasized that the soldiers were treated in accordance with the 1949 Geneva Convention and international humanitarian laws. The ICRC and ASEAN Observation Team (AOT) witnessed the handover, which Thailand hopes will build trust and lead to lasting peace.
title: แถลงการณ์กระทรวงการต่างประเทศเรื่องการส่งทหารกัมพูชา 18 คน กลับกัมพูชา
titleEn: Ministry of Foreign Affairs Statement on the Repatriation of 18 Cambodian Soldiers to Cambodia

summary: The Thai-Cambodian Border Situation Joint Information Center clarified the release of 18 Cambodian soldiers at the Ban Phakkad checkpoint in Chanthaburi. The move follows the General Border Committee (GBC) agreement, reflecting Thailand's stance on peaceful resolution and international humanitarian principles. The military emphasized that this does not compromise national sovereignty, as Thai forces remain on 24-hour high alert.
title: ศูนย์แถลงข่าวร่วมฯ แจงปมปล่อยตัว 18 ทหารกัมพูชา ยันไม่กระทบอธิปไตย-ความมั่นคง
titleEn: Joint Information Center clarifies release of 18 Cambodian soldiers, insists no impact on sovereignty or security

summary: Thai authorities oversaw the repatriation of 18 Cambodian soldiers at the Ban Phak Kat checkpoint in Chanthaburi on December 31. The move followed a successful 72-hour ceasefire monitoring period agreed upon during the General Border Committee (GBC) meeting. The process was observed by the ICRC and ASEAN teams to ensure it met international humanitarian standards and the Geneva Conventions.
title: Thailand repatriates 18 Cambodian soldiers after 72-hour border ceasefire

summary: The Second Army Region reports that the situation is under control with no heavy weaponry exchanges since the 72-hour ceasefire expired. However, Cambodian drone activity was spotted near Prasat Ta Kwai for reconnaissance, and troop reinforcements continue near Preah Vihear.
title: All is quiet on Cambodia border front
